main_text.p: funt Corvini)sed de talibus donis, ob quæ doctores inter se gloriabantur, puta linguarum, eloquentiæ, sapientiæ, quæ simpliciter pendebant à pura Dei donatione, & quod aliquis vel careat istis donis, vel ea parcius habeat, ad id nullum momentum adfert libertas voluntatis, cum contra in discretione fidelis ab infideli, ista libertas momentum' afferat. R. 1. Augustin. Chrysost. Cyprian. Concil. Aranfi[?]. can. 6. 3. Concili. Melivita[?] temporibus Honorii & Arcadii in Africa habitum, ita expofuerunt. 2.

Non stamus hominum authoritate, verum quidem est κατ' ἀρχὴν[?] non agi ib. de converfione hominis, neque nos eo fenfu textum urgemus, sed Apostolus ex majore universali, [Quis te discernit? quid gloriaris?] infert conclusio-nem, non gloriandum in donis divinitus collatis, & universaliter verum vult, neminem se dif-cernere, ne in donis gratiæ collatis. Hinc nos inferimus, multo minus gloriandum in nobis, de dono longè omnium excellentissimo & electorum proprio, nempe salutari ad Deum converfione in qua major laus, & gloria longè eminentior Deo debetur, quam in colla-tione donorum, quæ Deus reprobis etiam gratificari nonnunquam solet.

3. Ad hoc nullum momentum afferre libertatem huma-nam, quod careat, vel parcius habeat hæc dona, falsissimum est. Quod enim Apollos eloquentia & scripturarum peritia polleret, libertas ipsius in scripturarum lectione vale-bat,

page.notes: The text is set in one column. The page number reads 445 in the scan, with the final digit in a form resembling a long s. A small asterisk stands in the text after "quod careat"; it has no matching note on the page. The apostrophe after "momentum" is a printed mark and is kept as printed. The Greek phrase "κατ' ἀρχὴν" is doubtful in its accents and breathings. "Aranfi" and "Melivita" are doubtful names; they are read as printed and marked [?]. The bracketed sentence "[Quis te discernit? quid gloriaris?]" is printed in brackets and is kept as such. The text ends mid-word at "vale-bat," with a printed hyphen.
